repo_ai-specs.toml.content:
# ai-specs.toml — root manifest for the ai-specs standard.
#
# Single source of truth for: enabled agents, vendored skills (deps),
# MCP servers, and recipes. Local skills live under ai-specs/skills/<name>/
# and are autodiscovered — they are not listed here.

[project]
name = "ai-specs-cli"
subrepos = []

[agents]
# Supported agents: claude, cursor, opencode, codex, copilot, gemini, pi, omp
enabled = ["claude", "cursor", "opencode", "pi", "omp"]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Recipes — named bundles of skills, commands, templates, and MCP presets.
# Declared in catalog/recipes/<id>/recipe.toml. Sync uses the installed CLI
# catalog; no per-recipe version pin is required.
#
# [recipes.<id>]
# enabled = true
# # version = "1.0.0"  # legacy — ignored with WARN if present

# Flow primitives for this project come from these catalog recipes. Local
# skills under ai-specs/skills/ are limited to ai-specs' own bundled tooling
# (skill-creator, skill-sync); everything else of the flow is provided here
# plus the gentle-ai stack (SDD, memory).
#
# Recipes follow the capability model (see docs/capabilities.md):
#   foundational (consume capabilities): worktree-flow, git-pr-flow,
#     session-context, tdd-flow, plan-build-flow
#   specific (provide a capability): trello-mcp-workflow (tracker),
#     vault-canonical-store (canonical-store)
# Each capability has exactly one provider here, so sync auto-binds them; no
# explicit [[bindings]] are needed until a second provider is added (e.g. a
# jira recipe alongside trello — then bind `tracker` to one of them).

# --- Foundational ---

[recipes.worktree-flow]
enabled = true
[recipes.worktree-flow.config]
worktrees_dir = ".worktrees"
integration_branch = "epic/go-single-binary"
gate_mode="ask"
[recipes.git-pr-flow]
enabled = true
[recipes.git-pr-flow.config]
# Scoped to this branch: every card of the Go single-binary migration targets the
# epic integration branch, never development. The value travels with the branch,
# so a hotfix cut from development still resolves base_branch = "development".
base_branch = "epic/go-single-binary"
expected_owner = "parada1104"
auto_switch_account = true

[recipes.session-context]
enabled = true

[recipes.tdd-flow]
enabled = true
[recipes.tdd-flow.config]
test_command = "./tests/validate.sh"

[recipes.trello-mcp-workflow]
enabled = true
[recipes.trello-mcp-workflow.config]
board_id = "69ec097f13e2d38ecd89a557"
gate_mode = "warn"

default_list = "In Progress"
done_list = "Done"
reconcile = { scope_field = "board_id", max_age_seconds = 900, expectations = [{ event = "delivery", property = "list", config_field = "default_list" }, { event = "review", property = "list", config_field = "review_list" }, { event = "merge", property = "list", config_field = "done_list", config_field_when_set = "published_list" }] }
review_list = "Review"
[recipes.vault-canonical-store]
enabled = true
[recipes.vault-canonical-store.config]
vault_scope = "nnodes/proyectos/ai-specs"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Vendored skill dependencies — each [[deps]] entry is cloned by
# `ai-specs sync` into ai-specs/skills/<id>/ (gitignored).
#
# id                  (req) target directory under skills/
# source              (req) git URL (anything `git clone` accepts)
# path                (opt) subdirectory inside the repo where SKILL.md lives
# scope               (opt) default ["root"]
# auto_invoke         (opt) trigger phrases for the AGENTS.md Auto-invoke table
# license             (opt) SPDX identifier
# vendor_attribution  (opt) upstream author/org, cited in the skill description
# version             (opt) semantic version for metadata.version
#
# [[deps]]
# id = "tdd"
# source = "https://github.com/obra/superpowers"
# path = "skills/test-driven-development"
# license = "MIT"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Explicit capability bindings — only needed when multiple enabled recipes
# declare the same capability (to resolve ambiguity). With a single provider
# per capability, sync auto-binds them; no explicit [[bindings]] are needed.
#
# Example (uncomment to override auto-bind):
# [[bindings]]
# capability = "tracker"
# recipe = "trello-mcp-workflow"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MCP servers — distributed by sync-agent to each platform's native format.
# Environment variables are loaded from .envrc; agents interpolate at runtime
# (e.g. $TRELLO_API_KEY).
#
# All current servers come from recipe presets ([[provides.mcp]]):
#   trello          ← trello-mcp-workflow
#   vault-canonical ← vault-canonical-store (path via $CANONICAL_VAULT_PATH in .envrc)
# Declare [mcp.<name>] here only for ad-hoc servers without a recipe preset:
#
# [mcp.example]
# command = "npx"
# args = ["-y", "@example/mcp-server"]
# env = { EXAMPLE_TOKEN = "$EXAMPLE_TOKEN" }

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Runtime brief — prose sections for AGENTS.md generation.
# Structured values (board_id, integration_branch, test_command, vault_scope)
# come from recipe configs above. Only prose with no structured home lives here.

[brief]
intro = """
This is the project's director de orquesta: canonical runtime context for agents.
It covers project identity, MCPs, context sources, safety rules, and workflow conventions.
It does NOT track day-to-day work state — that lives in Trello and Engram.

**YOU ARE ON THE GO SINGLE-BINARY MIGRATION BRANCH, NOT development.**
This branch and every branch cut from it operate under the epic contract below.
Rules you may know from `development` do not all apply here: the integration
target is `epic/go-single-binary`, and nothing from this epic reaches
`development` until the whole migration is verified. Epic:
https://trello.com/c/qwlHQ7Xa
"""
purpose = "per-project AI harness for agent configuration, MCPs, recipes, memory, and tracker integration."
runtime_flow = [
  "A session works on one explicit user request or Trello card.",
  "The orchestrator coordinates work inline using project skills and the runtime brief.",
  "`explore` can run without a worktree when it only produces thinking.",
]
# The worktree requirement for protected-branch writes is contributed by the
# worktree-flow recipe (config-aware via `gate_mode`), not hard-coded here.
# "Trello is the source of truth..." is now contributed by trello-mcp-workflow recipe
# (key: trello-source-of-truth). Project-specific entries remain here.
context_sources = [
  "Specs and changes are tracked in the project's designated spec store (configurable per project).",
  "Vault is the canonical note-taker for decisions, handoffs, and structured project context.",
  "Engram is the operational memory layer for session facts, patterns, and short-lived continuity.",
  "Skills are executable guidance, not the primary contents of this runtime brief. Load specific skills by id when relevant (local under `ai-specs/skills/`, or CLI-bundled / recipe / dep via agent fan-out).",
  "Check Engram for the current active card and next recommended focus.",
]
# "Current explicit human instruction controls..." and "Tracker controls work state..."
# are now contributed by session-context recipe (keys: conflict-policy-source-authority,
# conflict-policy-source-hierarchy). Project-specific entries naming Trello/Vault remain.
conflict_policy = [
  "Skills define reusable procedures. Engram provides searchable operational context, not final authority.",
  "Proposed agent plans are lowest authority until accepted and recorded in Trello, Vault, docs, or code.",
]
# Most workflow rules are now contributed by worktree-flow, git-pr-flow, tdd-flow, and
# session-context recipes. Only project-specific rules remain here.
# worktree-flow already contributes: "Do not merge or push to `development` without a PR
# and explicit human instruction." — the version below adds the explicit-human-instruction
# emphasis for operations that bypass the PR (e.g. direct hotfix on dev).
workflow_rules = [
  "Follow the project's designated workflow for structured changes.",
  "Direct `skill-sync` runs are allowed only for metadata validation.",
  # Project-level Python→Go strangler policy (card #126). Incremental: apply at the seam you touch.
  "New authoritative logic, state machines, predicates, and durable state belong in Go.",
  "When touching Python on the active path, migrate the behavior/dependency being touched to Go where practical; Python may remain only as a thin compatibility/acquisition/JSON bridge during the transition.",
  "Keep one authoritative grader per behavior and add parity/contract tests at each migrated seam.",
  "Do not perform unrelated drive-by rewrites; the policy is incremental.",
  "EPIC CONTRACT — Go single-binary migration (https://trello.com/c/qwlHQ7Xa). This branch is the integration target for that epic. Card branches are cut FROM `epic/go-single-binary` and their PRs target it. No PR from this epic ever targets `development` or `main`.",
  "EPIC CONTRACT — Nothing from this epic reaches `development` while the epic is open. After all 16 cards are verified, ONE promotion PR is opened from card 16 (Cutover). Unrelated feature work continues on `development` in parallel and must not be disturbed.",
  "EPIC CONTRACT — TWO config values are deliberately scoped to this branch: `[recipes.git-pr-flow.config].base_branch` and `[recipes.worktree-flow.config].integration_branch`. BOTH MUST be reverted to `development` before the promotion PR, or every PR and worktree flow in the project starts targeting a deleted branch. Tracked as a blocking step on card 16.",
  "EPIC CONTRACT — New development moves toward the migration: no new Python modules under `lib/_internal/`, no new Bash logic in `lib/`, no new vendored Python under `lib/_vendor/`. New behavior in an already-ported area is written in Go; in a not-yet-ported area it must not deepen the Bash/Python surface.",
  "EPIC CONTRACT — Ported behavior is verified against `docs/go-migration-parity-contract.md`, which classifies every CLI surface FROZEN / TOLERANT / FREE. Do not 'fix' behavior recorded there as FROZEN, even when it looks wrong; recorded defects (D1-D35) are separate cards.",
  "DELEGATION — Orca workers own change content inside their assigned worktree only. A worker never stages, commits, pushes, merges, or manages worktree lifecycle; the canonical orchestrator owns those. See the `orca-aware-delegation` skill.",
  "DELEGATION — Never launch a worker headless (`pi -p`, `claude -p`, `opencode run`, provider API calls). Orca workers launch as visible interactive TUI sessions via `worker-start`.",
  "DELEGATION — `worker_done` never implies terminal closure by itself. Standing human decision for this epic: release once a worker completes its change cycle, since the PR lifecycle belongs to the orchestrator. Release only after an accepted `worker_done` — never on a timeout, idle TUI, heartbeat, question, escalation, or stale report — and retain anything that escalated, asked, or failed pending inspection.",
]# useful_commands_mode = "replace" keeps only the auto-generated test_command line and
# project-specific manual commands; suppresses recipe fragments that would duplicate
# the auto-generated "Full validation: ./tests/validate.sh" line.
useful_commands_mode = "replace"
useful_commands = [
  "Focused tests (unit-only): `./tests/run.sh`",
  "Inspect the active Trello card before resuming work.",
]

[brief.mcp_descriptions]
trello = "project tracking through the ai-specs-cli Roadmap board."
engram = "operational/session memory (global MCP)."
"vault-canonical" = "canonical project notes in the vault scoped to `nnodes/proyectos/ai-specs` (path from $CANONICAL_VAULT_PATH)."

write_dep_crlf.toml.content:
# Write-corpus fixture: CRLF manifest with two [[deps]] blocks for
# first-of-two removal; output must come out LF-normalized on both sides.
[agents]
enabled = ["claude"]

[[deps]]
id = "first"
source = "u"

[[deps]]
id = "second"
source = "v"

write_dep_guard.toml.content:
# Write-corpus fixture: VALID TOML whose dep removal regresses to invalid
# (same multi-line-array segmenter trick as write_recipe_guard.toml).
[[deps]]
id = "doom"
items = [
["x"],
]

[after]
y = 1

write_dep_invalid_base.toml.content:
# Write-corpus fixture: ALREADY-INVALID TOML dep case — removal proceeds.
[[deps]]
id = "x"
broken = =

write_deps_two.toml.content:
# Write-corpus fixture: two [[deps]] blocks; removal must take exactly one.
# comment

[project]
name = "deps-test"

[[deps]]
id = "first"
source = "git::https://example.com/first"
scope = ["root"]

[[deps]]
id = "second"
source = "git::https://example.com/second"
scope = ["x", "y"]

write_recipe_basic.toml.content:
# Write-corpus fixture: recipes with sub-tables (config) for segment removal.
[project]
name = "write-test"

[recipes.a]
enabled = true

[recipes.a.config]
k = "v"

[recipes.b]
enabled = false

write_recipe_crlf.toml.content:
# Write-corpus fixture: CRLF manifest for segment removal. python's
# read_text translates CRLF to LF in memory, so the round-trip output is
# LF-normalized on both sides — including inside multi-line strings.
[project]
name = "crlf-test"

[recipes.a]
enabled = true
desc = """
multi
line
"""

[recipes.a.config]
k = "v"

[recipes.b]
enabled = false

write_recipe_crlf_guard.toml.content:
# Write-corpus fixture: CRLF manifest whose removal regresses to invalid.
# The valid→invalid guard refuses, so the ORIGINAL CRLF bytes must stay
# untouched on disk on both sides (the heredoc exits before writing).
[recipes.doom]
items = [
["x"],
]

[after]
y = 1

write_recipe_guard.toml.content:
# Write-corpus fixture: VALID TOML whose removal regresses to invalid.
# The multi-line array contains column-0 '[' lines, which the segmenter
# treats as headers; removing the [recipes.doom] header segment orphans the
# array lines and the valid→invalid guard must fire.
[recipes.doom]
items = [
["x"],
]

[after]
y = 1

write_recipe_invalid_base.toml.content:
# Write-corpus fixture: ALREADY-INVALID TOML — removal proceeds because the
# guard only refuses a valid→invalid regression.
[recipes.x]
enabled = true
broken = =

# ai-specs.toml — root manifest for the ai-specs standard.
#
# Single source of truth for: enabled agents, vendored skills (deps),
# MCP servers, and recipes. Local skills live under ai-specs/skills/<name>/
# and are autodiscovered — they are not listed here.

[project]
name = "ai-specs-cli"
subrepos = []

[agents]
# Supported agents: claude, cursor, opencode, codex, copilot, gemini, pi, omp
enabled = ["claude", "cursor", "opencode", "pi", "omp"]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Recipes — named bundles of skills, commands, templates, and MCP presets.
# Declared in catalog/recipes/<id>/recipe.toml. Sync uses the installed CLI
# catalog; no per-recipe version pin is required.
#
# [recipes.<id>]
# enabled = true
# # version = "1.0.0"  # legacy — ignored with WARN if present

# Flow primitives for this project come from these catalog recipes. Local
# skills under ai-specs/skills/ are limited to ai-specs' own bundled tooling
# (skill-creator, skill-sync); everything else of the flow is provided here
# plus the gentle-ai stack (SDD, memory).
#
# Recipes follow the capability model (see docs/capabilities.md):
#   foundational (consume capabilities): worktree-flow, git-pr-flow,
#     session-context, tdd-flow, plan-build-flow
#   specific (provide a capability): trello-mcp-workflow (tracker),
#     vault-canonical-store (canonical-store)
# Each capability has exactly one provider here, so sync auto-binds them; no
# explicit [[bindings]] are needed until a second provider is added (e.g. a
# jira recipe alongside trello — then bind `tracker` to one of them).

# --- Foundational ---

[recipes.git-pr-flow]
enabled = true
[recipes.git-pr-flow.config]
# Scoped to this branch: every card of the Go single-binary migration targets the
# epic integration branch, never development. The value travels with the branch,
# so a hotfix cut from development still resolves base_branch = "development".
base_branch = "epic/go-single-binary"
expected_owner = "parada1104"
auto_switch_account = true

[recipes.session-context]
enabled = true

[recipes.tdd-flow]
enabled = true
[recipes.tdd-flow.config]
test_command = "./tests/validate.sh"

[recipes.trello-mcp-workflow]
enabled = true
[recipes.trello-mcp-workflow.config]
board_id = "69ec097f13e2d38ecd89a557"
gate_mode = "warn"

default_list = "In Progress"
done_list = "Done"
reconcile = { scope_field = "board_id", max_age_seconds = 900, expectations = [{ event = "delivery", property = "list", config_field = "default_list" }, { event = "review", property = "list", config_field = "review_list" }, { event = "merge", property = "list", config_field = "done_list", config_field_when_set = "published_list" }] }
review_list = "Review"
[recipes.vault-canonical-store]
enabled = true
[recipes.vault-canonical-store.config]
vault_scope = "nnodes/proyectos/ai-specs"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Vendored skill dependencies — each [[deps]] entry is cloned by
# `ai-specs sync` into ai-specs/skills/<id>/ (gitignored).
#
# id                  (req) target directory under skills/
# source              (req) git URL (anything `git clone` accepts)
# path                (opt) subdirectory inside the repo where SKILL.md lives
# scope               (opt) default ["root"]
# auto_invoke         (opt) trigger phrases for the AGENTS.md Auto-invoke table
# license             (opt) SPDX identifier
# vendor_attribution  (opt) upstream author/org, cited in the skill description
# version             (opt) semantic version for metadata.version
#
# [[deps]]
# id = "tdd"
# source = "https://github.com/obra/superpowers"
# path = "skills/test-driven-development"
# license = "MIT"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Explicit capability bindings — only needed when multiple enabled recipes
# declare the same capability (to resolve ambiguity). With a single provider
# per capability, sync auto-binds them; no explicit [[bindings]] are needed.
#
# Example (uncomment to override auto-bind):
# [[bindings]]
# capability = "tracker"
# recipe = "trello-mcp-workflow"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MCP servers — distributed by sync-agent to each platform's native format.
# Environment variables are loaded from .envrc; agents interpolate at runtime
# (e.g. $TRELLO_API_KEY).
#
# All current servers come from recipe presets ([[provides.mcp]]):
#   trello          ← trello-mcp-workflow
#   vault-canonical ← vault-canonical-store (path via $CANONICAL_VAULT_PATH in .envrc)
# Declare [mcp.<name>] here only for ad-hoc servers without a recipe preset:
#
# [mcp.example]
# command = "npx"
# args = ["-y", "@example/mcp-server"]
# env = { EXAMPLE_TOKEN = "$EXAMPLE_TOKEN" }
